newsitem.title: NEPAL: South Asia trade talks to conclude by December.
newsitem.headline: South Asia trade talks to conclude by December.

text.p: Negotiators from South Asian nations agreed on Thursday to conclude a third round of talks on cutting tariffs within the region by December, officials said.

"They (the negotiators) decided to conclude the third round of the South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) negotiations by December 1997," an official of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) said.
Ashok K. Attri, director of Kathmandu-based SAARC secretariat, told Reuters that delegates from the seven SAARC member nations had exchanged lists of products for trade concessions.
The group's members -- Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka -- will hold two more rounds of talks before enlarging the list of products for tariff cuts, Attri said.
SAARC was formed in 1985 to improve the economies of the South Asian nations, which together hold more than one fifth of the world's population.
Under SAPTA, member countries have agreed to cut tariffs on over 2,000 items by between 10 and 100 percent. The least-developed member countries are entitled to additional tariff concessions.
"Delegations were of the view that substantial progress will be achieved to enlarge the SAPTA concessions significantly," Attri said without elaborating.

The number of new products qualifying for additional tariff concessions and the fresh duty cuts will be finalised only when the negotiations conclude, he said. Officials earlier said tariffs would be slashed on up to 3,000 products.

Negotiators said the tariff reductions aimed to bolster trade between the South Asian nations, which currently represents only 3.4 percent of total global trade, and to launch a South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) by 2001.
